precepts.text: Is he the God of the Jews only? Is he not also of the Gentiles? Is he only for the southern kingdom? He is also the God of the northern kingdom: one God which shall justify the circumcision by faith, and uncircumcision through faith.
precepts.point: If ye then be risen with Christ, seek those things which are above. If you decide to repent and follow Christ, this is now what you do. But if you do not want to accept Christ, it is not for you. All Israel is not Israel, as it says in Romans 9:6.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
Galatians says “a mediator is not a mediator of one, but God is one.” Romans explains it: “Is he the God of the Jews only?” Is he only for the southern kingdom? “Is he not also of the Gentiles?” Is he not also the God of the northern kingdom? “Yes, of the Gentiles also.”

“Seeing it is one God, which shall justify the circumcision by faith, and uncircumcision through faith.” The circumcision is Judah, the southern kingdom; the uncircumcision is the northern kingdom. One God justifies both, by faith.

That is who Colossians 3:1 is speaking to: “If ye then be risen with Christ.” Both houses of Israel, Jew and Gentile, who believe on Christ are risen with him, and the promise by faith of Jesus Christ is given to them that believe.

precepts.text: Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood. Propitiation means atonement.
precepts.point: The day of atonement: on the tenth day of the seventh month ye shall afflict your souls. Christ was that atonement.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Paul names what Christ is: “Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood”. God sent Christ forth, and propitiation means atonement.

He was set forth “to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God”. The sins that are past are forgiven through faith in his blood, by God’s forbearance toward us.

So the day of atonement, when Israel afflicted their souls and brought an offering by fire, finds its meaning in Christ. He is the atonement God himself set forth, and we receive it through faith in his blood.

precepts.text: If thou hast understanding, answer thy neighbour; if not, lay thy hand upon thy mouth. When you do not know, shut up. Do not freestyle; speak truth to your neighbour. You can look composed and unbothered and still not know what you are talking about.
precepts.point: As it is written is where we live. When someone asks why I have one wife, I take them to the scripture where the Lord said one wife, no remix, no loophole.

note.label: Fixx Ya Face Fridays | as Was Supposed!!

precepts.why:
“Let God be true, but every man a liar; as it is written”. As it is written is where we stay and where we live, and we are not budging from it. Whenever we say something God said, we go back to the scripture and justify ourselves with thus saith the Lord. If you do it any other way, you are evil.

Sirach shows what to do when you do not have the scripture for it: “If thou hast understanding, answer thy neighbour; if not, lay thy hand upon thy mouth.” When you are asked a question and you understand, and you know where in the Bible it is, give answer. If you do not know, shut up. That is what laying your hand upon your mouth means. It is best to be quiet.

You do not get to freestyle or go off the top of your head. You have to speak truth to your neighbour; that is the law. I don’t care how composed you look or how unbothered you make yourself appear; if you don’t know what you’re talking about, shut up. Pride steps in, and brothers get frazzled but will not let you know it.

That is what happened with Luke 3:23, “being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph, which was the son of Heli”. Someone did not know, so he made up that Jacob and Heli were brothers and pulled in levirate marriage, when the “as was supposed” was about Christ being the son of Joseph and had nothing to do with Heli. Lay Luke 3 beside Matthew 1 and they are two different lineages: Matthew follows Joseph, Luke follows Mary. Nowhere does the Bible say Jacob and Heli were brothers. Let God be true and keep it as it is written; where you have no scripture, lay your hand upon your mouth.

precepts.text: In every work that he began in the service of the house of God, and in the law and in the commandments, to seek his God. Verse 2: Hezekiah appointed the priests and Levites to their courses to do the works of God in the temple. Those are the works.
precepts.point: You cannot boast in sacrificing as though it makes you special, because it is done; Christ died for us. Justification is through Christ, and it is in the same chapter as let God be true and every man a liar.

note.label: Fixx Ya Face Fridays | as Was Supposed!!

precepts.why:
“Where is boasting then? It is excluded. By what law? of works? Nay: but by the law of faith.” What are the works Paul is talking about? Not what your son did today while you were at work. One so-called leader stood up and asked a room if you go home and ask your son what his deeds were today. Who does that? He is an idiot, and whoever listens to him needs to repent.

Chronicles shows what the works are: “And in every work that he began in the service of the house of God, and in the law, and in the commandments, to seek his God, he did it with all his heart, and prospered.” The works are the works done in the service of the house of God: the sacrificial law.

Earlier in the same chapter, “Hezekiah appointed the courses of the priests and the Levites after their courses, every man according to his service, the priests and Levites for burnt offerings and for peace offerings”. Those are the works of God in the temple.

So when Paul says boasting is excluded, it means you cannot boast that you are sacrificing, as though it makes you something special, because that is done: Christ died for us. The justification is through Christ, by faith, not by the works of the temple service.

precepts.text: Nehemiah contended that the house of God was forsaken, gathered the tithe of corn, wine, and oil into the treasuries, set faithful treasurers, and prayed, wipe not out my good deeds. The deeds were the sacrifices and offerings brought to the house.
precepts.point: You cannot boast in sacrificing as though it makes you special, because it is done; Christ died for us. Justification is through Christ, and it is in the same chapter as let God be true and every man a liar.

note.label: Fixx Ya Face Fridays | as Was Supposed!!

precepts.why:
“Therefore we conclude that a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law.” What are the deeds of the law? Nehemiah shows them: “Then contended I with the rulers, and said, Why is the house of God forsaken? And I gathered them together, and set them in their place.” We are talking about the house of God.

“Then brought all Judah the tithe of the corn and the new wine and the oil unto the treasuries.” This is what they brought: the offerings. He “made treasurers over the treasuries, Shelemiah the priest, and Zadok the scribe, and of the Levites, Pedaiah”, “for they were counted faithful, and their office was to distribute unto their brethren.”

“Remember me, O my God, concerning this, and wipe not out my good deeds that I have done for the house of my God, and for the offices thereof.” The deeds were the sacrifices and offerings he brought to the house of God.

And it is in the same chapter of Romans where God is justified in his sayings and overcomes when he is judged: let God be true, and every man a liar. This is serious. Your salvation is at hand, and a teacher who is up at the podium drinking, talking about sex and baby oil and prostitution, instead of instructing the people what these scriptures are talking about, is not a leader to lead people to God. He is a joke.

precepts.why:
This is one of the first scriptures we learned when we came into this truth, elementary but important: “Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth.” An elder has men under him who look to him for wisdom, knowledge and understanding. The brother who said a man’s deeds are what his son did today embarrassed the hell out of himself and his organization. Now he is being clowned, and because he represents the Israelite community, they label us all as stupid. And never trust a man wearing dark sunglasses inside: he can hide his embarrassment and his eyes. Brother, you have to repent and change your ways.

“But shun profane and vain babblings: for they will increase unto more ungodliness.” That is profane and vain babbling; it doesn’t make any sense. And nobody in the room, nobody equal to his rank, says, hey, listen, brother, next time. He keeps having a pattern of doing the same thing.

Here, if a captain starts talking crazy, a captain junior to him is going to correct him, because we represent Israel United in Christ, and our elders have taught us with knowledge, wisdom and understanding how to conduct ourselves. There are checks and balances. That brother does not have any of that, and so he cannot rightly divide Romans 3.

precepts.text: What thing shall I liken to thee, O daughter of Jerusalem? for thy breach is great like the sea: who can heal thee? A breach is a split or a tear, and the root of reparations is repair. Isaiah 58:11-12: the Lord shall guide thee continually and satisfy thy soul in drought; they that shall be of thee shall build the old waste places, and thou shalt be called, The repairer of the breach, the restorer of paths to dwell in. Our souls in drought will be watered and healed.
precepts.point: Sin is the transgression of the law, 1 John 3:4. Now we know that what things soever the law saith, it saith to them who are under the law: those under the law break it and are under sin, and both Jews and Gentiles under sin means both under the law, which the other nations never were. That every mouth may be stopped, and all the world may become guilty before God, the world that received God's commandments under Moses. Therefore by the deeds of the law, sacrifice, there shall no flesh be justified in his sight, for we are justified by Christ's blood; for by the law is the knowledge of sin, because to acknowledge a sin, willful or ignorant, you had to bring an animal.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

precepts.why:
Paul proves from the Psalms that Israel became filthy: “They are all gone aside, they are all together become filthy: there is none that doeth good, no, not one.” The whole nation was broken. Jeremiah laments that same breaking: “What thing shall I liken to thee, O daughter of Jerusalem? what shall I equal to thee, that I may comfort thee, O virgin daughter of Zion? for thy breach is great like the sea: who can heal thee?”

A breach is a split or a tear. Our breach is great like the sea. Who can heal us? Christ, our saviour.

Isaiah shows the healing: “And the Lord shall guide thee continually, and satisfy thy soul in drought, and make fat thy bones: and thou shalt be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water, whose waters fail not.” When our souls are in drought, the Lord is going to water us and heal us. “And they that shall be of thee shall build the old waste places”, the waste places we made when we became filthy. “Thou shalt raise up the foundations of many generations; and thou shalt be called, The repairer of the breach, The restorer of paths to dwell in.”

The root word of reparations is repair. The repairer of the breach: that is the reparations right there. Both Jews and Gentiles, Judah and Ephraim, were “all under sin” and torn apart, and the one who heals that breach is Christ, repairing and restoring Israel.

Build again is the reconciliation and the reparation of all twelve tribes. Then verse 17: that the residue of men, the rest of the nations, might seek after the Lord, and all the Gentiles upon whom my name is called, the Christians, who try to include themselves in our restoration and adoption.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

precepts.why:
Paul says “we have before proved both Jews and Gentiles, that they are all under sin”, and the Gentiles there are Israelites. Acts 15 shows the same Gentiles being restored: “Simeon hath declared how God at the first did visit the Gentiles, to take out of them a people for his name.” That references what took place in Acts 10, and we understand that is talking about Israel.

“And to this agree the words of the prophets; as it is written, After this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down; and I will build again the ruins thereof, and I will set it up”. Build again: that is the reconciliation, that is the reparation. It had fallen down because we became filthy, and God restores the waste places. Who is that? All twelve tribes of Israel.

Then verse 17: “That the residue of men might seek after the Lord”. The residue is the rest of the nations outside of the twelve tribes: Edom and the others. “And all the Gentiles, upon whom my name is called”: that is the Christians, and the Jews.

They try to include themselves in our reconciliation, our restoration and our adoption. But the building again is of David’s tabernacle, the twelve tribes; the residue only seeks after the Lord once Israel is set up again.

precepts.text: In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof, and raise up his ruins, and build it as in the days of old, that they may possess the remnant of Edom, and of all the heathen which are called by my name. The twelve tribes possess Edom and the heathen called by his name; other nations cannot be part of our reconciliation, restoration, or reparation.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

precepts.why:
Acts 15 quotes the prophet Amos: “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof”. The breaches are the tear, the split, like the breach “great like the sea” in Lamentations. Remember, the root word of reparations is to repair.

“And I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old”. This is the restoring of Israel, both kingdoms that Paul proved “are all under sin” in Romans 3, repaired and raised up as in the days of old.

Then: “That they may possess the remnant of Edom, and of all the heathen, which are called by my name, saith the Lord that doeth this.” That they, all twelve tribes, may possess the remnant of Edom and of the heathen called by his name.

So you see, other nations cannot be involved in our reconciliation, our restoration or our reparation. The ones called by his name, the Christians and the Jews, are not the tabernacle being raised; they are what Israel possesses once it is raised. This goes back to the classes before on Romans 11 and Acts 10.

note.label: Deuteronomy 9: Not for Thy Righteousness

precepts.why:
“There is no fear of God before their eyes.” Religion removed the fear and austerity of the Most High from before us, and this is the result.

Look at the Most High here: “Let me alone, that I may destroy them, and blot out their name from under heaven: and I will make of thee a nation mightier and greater than they.” He was ready to go back to the days of the flood and start over with one man; time means nothing to the Ancient of days. That is the fierceness, the wrath and the severity of the Most High.

Religion has tried to remove all of that and push an effeminate white Jesus in front of us that loves everybody, forgives everything at the last breath with no commandments kept, and can do no wrong. We are suffering in all our cities, in Africa, in Europe and in the Caribbean from that lack of fear of God before our eyes.

precepts.text: Shall the unbelief of some make the faith of God without effect? God forbid; let God be true, but every man a liar, that Job be justified in his sayings.
precepts.point: And if it be not so now, who will make Job a liar and make his speech nothing worth? The prophecy will come true because Job is speaking as the mouthpiece of God.

note.label: Job 24: The Crimes of the Oppressor

precepts.why:
Job ends, “And if it be not so now, who will make me a liar, and make my speech nothing worth?” Paul answers: “For what if some did not believe? shall their unbelief make the faith of God without effect? God forbid: yea, let God be true, but every man a liar; as it is written, That thou mightest be justified in thy sayings, and mightest overcome when thou art judged.”

Job is speaking as the mouthpiece of God, so the prophecy will come true. The unbelief of some cannot make the faith of God without effect. Let God be true and every man a liar, that Job be justified in his sayings: the wicked are exalted for a little while, then gone and brought low, taken out of the way and cut off as the tops of the ears of corn.

precepts.text: There is none that understandeth, there is none that seeketh after God; their throat is an open sepulchre, with their tongues they have used deceit, the poison of asps is under their lips. This describes the same wicked mouths David speaks of in Psalm 5:9.
precepts.point: For there is no faithfulness in their mouth; their inward part is very wickedness; their throat is an open sepulchre; they flatter with their tongue. The enemies are full of wickedness and deceit, flattering with their tongues.

note.label: Psalm 5: For Thou Lord Wilt Bless the Righteous

precepts.why:
Paul describes the same wicked mouths David speaks of: “There is none that understandeth, there is none that seeketh after God. They are all gone out of the way, they are together become unprofitable; there is none that doeth good, no, not one.” Then he uses David's very words: “Their throat is an open sepulchre; with their tongues they have used deceit; the poison of asps is under their lips”.

This is why David asks, “Lead me, O Lord, in thy righteousness because of mine enemies”. The enemies watching him have no faithfulness in their mouth; their inward part is very wickedness, and they flatter with their tongue. What comes out of their throat is death, like an open grave, and deceit and poison sit under their lips. Because of enemies like that David needs the Most High to make his way straight before his face.

precepts.text: Just because we do not believe does not make the faith of God without effect; our unbelief does not make the Bible untrue.
precepts.point: We are not going to stand before the Most High and be justified talking about "me and Jesus." If any man speak, let him speak as the oracles of God. Wearing pants, not wearing fringes, crossdressing; none of that will be excused.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why:
“For what if some did not believe? shall their unbelief make the faith of God without effect?” Just because we do not believe does not make the faith of God without effect. Our unbelief does not make the Bible untrue.

David sinned against the Most High only, and he says it was “that thou mightest be justified when thou speakest, and be clear when thou judgest.” The Most High is justified whether man believes him or not. We are not going to stand before him and be justified talking about me and Jesus; his word stands, and it is our belief that has to line up with it.

If any man speak, let him speak as the oracles of God.

We will not stand before the Most High and be justified talking about me and Jesus. Wearing pants, not wearing fringes, crossdressing: none of that will be excused. He is justified when he speaks and clear when he judges, and every man who says otherwise is a liar.

precepts.text: What advantage hath the Jew, or profit of circumcision? Much every way, chiefly because to them were committed the oracles of God.
precepts.point: So the circumcision was primarily the southern kingdom, Judah, raised in the law, and the Pharisees who pushed circumcision above everything, even above faith and the commandments; the uncircumcision was the northern kingdom and the scattered Israelites.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
“What advantage then hath the Jew? or what profit is there of circumcision? Much every way: chiefly, because that unto them were committed the oracles of God.”

The circumcision, Judah, had the advantage of being raised in the law, because unto them were committed the oracles of God. That is why they held themselves apart from the uncircumcision and contended with Peter for eating with them.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
“What advantage then hath the Jew? or what profit is there of circumcision?” The Jews were called the circumcision because they kept the covenant of circumcision established to Abraham.

The circumcision was the southern kingdom of Judah, Benjamin and Levi. The uncircumcised were primarily the northern kingdom. That is why Peter's apostleship was “of the circumcision” and Paul's was toward the Gentiles, the uncircumcision.

points: We have before proved both Jews and Gentiles, that they are all under sin. Uh oh, they got us, Jews and Gentiles. But where do you prove it? Not from Paul's letters; from the law and the prophets he cited. Show me the nations by name, Moab, Ammon, Ishmael, that were under the old covenant with us; not individuals of the mixed multitude, nations. It is not there, so the Gentiles under sin must be a nation called Gentiles: Israelites.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

points: As it is written, there is none righteous, no, not one; Psalms 14:2-3, the Lord looked down upon the children of men and they are all gone aside, altogether become filthy. There is none that understandeth, none that seeketh after God; they are all gone out of the way, they are together become unprofitable: both kingdoms, Ephraim and Judah, evil as hell, proven in Kings and Hosea 1. Their throat is an open sepulchre, Psalms 10:7, cursing and deceit; their feet are swift to shed blood, and the way of peace have they not known, Isaiah 59:7-8, spoken of Israel; there is no fear of God before their eyes, Psalms 36:1. All of us together were wicked.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

points: Sin is the transgression of the law, 1 John 3:4. Now we know that what things soever the law saith, it saith to them who are under the law: those under the law break it and are under sin, and both Jews and Gentiles under sin means both under the law, which the other nations never were. That every mouth may be stopped, and all the world may become guilty before God, the world that received God's commandments under Moses. Therefore by the deeds of the law, sacrifice, there shall no flesh be justified in his sight, for we are justified by Christ's blood; for by the law is the knowledge of sin, because to acknowledge a sin, willful or ignorant, you had to bring an animal.
